items.title: 20.2 Diagnostic Use of Ultrasound in Medical Imaging

source_refs.note: Topic 20.2 with boxes (PDF 158-159); Fig 20.2 (machine photograph and probe drawing) is redrawn as a schematic. The d = vt/2 relation and the echo calculation are added for the learning outcome; answer needs review.

blocks.text: Ultrasound lets doctors view internal body structures in real time (Fig 20.2 shows an ultrasound machine). A transducer sends high-frequency sound waves, typically 1 MHz to 15 MHz, into the body. The waves travel through the body and are reflected at boundaries between different tissues; the echoes are collected and analysed to build an image. A key advantage is that ultrasound uses no ionising radiation, so it is safe, non-invasive and can be repeated.

The piezoelectric transducer emits pulses of ultrasound, which travel at different speeds in different tissues. When a wave meets a boundary between two tissues of different acoustic impedance (set by the tissue's density and the speed of sound in it), part of the wave is reflected. The transducer then switches to receive mode and detects the reflected waves by the direct piezoelectric effect. The echoes become electrical signals; a computer uses the time delay and the strength of each echo to build an image. Stronger reflections appear brighter, revealing the internal structure of organs and tissues.

items: Acoustic impedance difference: a larger difference between two tissues (for example soft tissue and bone) gives stronger echoes and clearer boundaries.
Frequency of ultrasound: higher frequency gives better resolution but less penetration; lower frequency penetrates deeper but gives a less clear image.
Use of gel: a special gel between the transducer and the skin removes air gaps and improves the transmission of sound waves.

blocks.text: Ultrasound is used in many medical specialties. In obstetrics it monitors fetal growth, estimates gestational age and identifies abnormalities during pregnancy. In the abdomen it examines the liver, kidneys, gallbladder, pancreas and bladder. In cardiology, echocardiography shows the heart's structure and function in real time. In urology it examines the prostate, testicles and urinary system, and in the musculoskeletal system it helps detect ligament injuries, joint inflammation and other soft-tissue conditions.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: The crystals in an ultrasound probe are smaller than a grain of rice, but they can both send and detect sound waves. Ultrasound can even measure the speed of blood flow, using the Doppler effect to detect shifts in sound frequency.
